documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: VIN, window sticker photo, Carfax summary with 22 entries and consistent mileage, clean title claimed, one-family chain. Maintenance evidence is partial: records exist only since 2022, the VVT campaign is relayed by the seller rather than shown, and no invoices were examined here.

condition.rationale: Several disclosed faults: cracked dash, moisture in the headlights, intermittent backup camera, rear pads at 10%, chrome wheel corrosion, and 2012 door bodywork. These are offset by low mileage, a clean engine bay, a dry-looking rear underbody photo, and a claimed 2025 rack and 2026 belts and idlers, none of which are receipted here.

price_value.rationale: No fair value estimate or comps were provided. Market notes put documented low-mile cars at high-single to mid-teens, and commenters expect low teens. The known work list (dash, headlights, camera, rear brakes) is several thousand dollars and must come off any hammer price.

mission_fit.rationale: The mission requires capability the household's 2018 RX 350 does not supply. A 2007 RX 350 AWD is an older version of the same vehicle, with no added sleeping-platform, rooftop-tent or off-pavement capability beyond roof rails and tow prep. This is the 'second Lexus SUV' the profile deprioritizes.

logistics.rationale: Seattle is a flight plus a long drive from Carmel. The seller actively offers in-person viewing, but only about 24 hours remain to arrange a PPI before the no-reserve close. California smog for a 2007 gas car should be feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: One-family ownership with the window sticker, Premium Plus and Towing Prep, AWD, and Crystal White over Ivory with low miles make it a nicer-than-typical example. It is otherwise an ordinary RX.

ppi_focus: Confirm the VVT-i oil feed line at the rear of the engine is the all-metal 9LH part; inspect the oil cooler lines.
Check the water pump weep hole for pink crust, and check coolant condition and level.
Check the new steering rack boots and the pressure/return hoses for seepage; check for groaning at full lock.
Check the PTU output seal and vent, the rear diff seals, propshaft center bearing and CV boots; check PTU fluid condition.
Road test the U151E for 2–3/3–4 flare, engagement delay, and converter shudder at 40–50 mph.
Run a full module scan (engine, transmission, ABS/VSC, SRS, AFS) and check readiness monitors.
Inspect the headlight housings for moisture and seal failure; check AFS swivel and HID function.
Check paint depth and panel fit on the left-rear door, and check for overspray.
Inspect the front lower control arm bushings, sway links and strut mounts; read tire date codes and wear pattern.
Diagnose the backup camera fault, and check the dash crack's proximity to the airbag seam.
what_would_change_verdict: A clear capability case versus the existing RX (for example, a defined sleeping-platform or rooftop-tent plan this car enables) would raise mission fit; absent that, this car duplicates the household's current vehicle.
A dealer-history printout confirming 9LH plus invoices for the rack and transmission service would lift documentation.
A clean pre-close PPI with dry front underside and no codes would raise condition; a wet PTU, pump seepage or AFS faults would lower it.
A hammer price rising well into the mid-teens, combined with the known work list, would erode value.
evidence.mission_note: This is a newer-mileage example of essentially the same vehicle Jason already owns. It adds no camping or capability the 2018 RX 350 lacks, so it does not satisfy the utility_capability brief, and accelerated_bridge mode does not need a second RX.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly, the window sticker photo matches the claimed packages and price, and the Carfax summary agrees with the 59k miles and one-family ownership. The seller relays a Lexus dealer record of the 9LH VVT-i hose campaign at 17,863 miles; this is credible but not yet shown as a document. The seller discloses a cracked dash, moisture in the headlight assemblies, an intermittent backup camera, rear pads at 10%, chrome wheel corrosion, and 2012 left-rear door bodywork that Carfax does not report. Recent work is claimed (rack and power steering flush 2025, transmission service 2025, belts and idlers 2026), but records before 2022 were discarded, and nothing is said about coolant, PTU or rear diff fluids, tire dates, or a code scan. The photos show a clean engine bay and a dry rear underbody; the front underside was not examined here. Several attached photos (NSX, 718, G-Class, GMC pickup) are unrelated to this car and were ignored. Functionally, the car duplicates the household's existing RX 350 rather than adding capability.
evidence.next_action: Before deciding whether to bid, ask the seller today for the Lexus owner-portal history printout, the 2025 rack and transmission invoices, the tire date codes, and permission for a Seattle-area PPI before the 2026-10-15 11:24 close.
